# The CI scope classifier that gates every test run has no unit spec

Sub of #17922 · sibling of #17924, #17964, #17968 · covers the fix shipped by #16289

## Context

`c623b2f63c` (#17791 via #17806) deleted 804 unit spec files on the `test/playwright/unit/ai/**` path prefix. #17922 censused the 30 under `ai/buildScripts/` and found **27 whose subject never left this repository**. Twenty-one recover verbatim and landed in #17924 / PR #17925. Six were tabled with a named cause each.

**Two of those six are already delivered**, measured at `dev@40edf8abfa`:

| tabled residual | actual state |
|---|---|
| AC-4, the `check-spec-retirement` narrowing | **DONE** — `f189cc6ffa` (#17964, CLOSED) shipped `deriveSubjectSuffix`, `findSurvivingSubjects`, `unaccountedSurvivors` |
| `DataSyncPipeline.spec.mjs` | **RESTORED** — `f809d86e29` (#17920 / #17927), now at `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.spec.mjs` |

So #17922's owed set is **5, not 6**. This ticket takes the first of the five.

## The Problem

`util/WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` (237 lines) covered the `jobs.changes` `scope` step in `.github/workflows/test.yml`. That step is not a module — it is an inline `actions/github-script` body — and it **runs on every pull request and decides whether `unit` and `components` execute at all**.

`neomjs/neo` CI is exactly those two projects. So a classifier that answers `false` too eagerly does not turn anything red: it produces a green run with nothing behind it. That is the same failure #17922 exists about, one layer above the specs that ticket restores — and the classifier has had **zero** coverage since 2026-08-27.

**What is uncovered right now**, all read from the live script at `dev@40edf8abfa`:

| behavior | consequence if it silently breaks |
|---|---|
| `isCurrentPullRequestHead` stale-head guard | a superseded attempt classifies against a diff that is not the head's |
| fail-toward-running on an undeterminable `package.json` diff (fetch / parse / missing base ref) | the optimization starts skipping suites it cannot reason about |
| fork-PR head content resolved from `pull_request.head.repo` | **every fork PR fails open into full suites forever** — this is precisely the fix #16289 shipped, and it has been unguarded since the sweep |
| `requiresUnitForContent` (`resources/content/release-notes/`, `.../discussions/`, `apps/portal/resources/data/`, `learn/`) | the corpus gate is skipped on exactly the PRs it exists to catch |
| `isComponentsRelevantPath` including `.github/workflows/test.yml` | a scoping regression ships on the one PR guaranteed not to exercise it |

Note the third row: #16289 is CLOSED COMPLETED, its fix is live, and the only spec asserting it was deleted five days later by an unrelated commit. The fix is correct today by inspection and by nothing else.

## Why this one is a rewrite, not a restoration

#17922 tables this spec as *"expects `run_integration` / `run_components` admissions the classifier no longer makes post-split"*. Confirmed mechanically rather than inherited:

```
$ node -e "…yaml.load('.github/workflows/test.yml').jobs.changes.outputs"
{ run_unit, run_components, skip_reason }
```

`run_integration` and `run_parity` are **gone** — both suites left with the extraction. Seven of the nine deleted arms assert them, so a verbatim restore reds on seven arms for a reason that has nothing to do with the classifier being wrong. That is a legitimate topology change in the subject, and dropping those keys is re-aiming, not trimming — which is why AC-3 below requires it to be stated in the file rather than done quietly.

The harness itself — reading the committed script string out of the YAML and evaluating it with `AsyncFunction` against mocked `github` / `context` / `core` — reconciles cleanly and is what makes the subject testable at all.

## The Fix

1. Restore to `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/`, beside the surviving sibling tree — **not** the old `unit/ai/` path, whose prefix is what classified it as extracted substrate and would re-arm the same deletion at the next boundary change.
2. Re-aim the seven arms onto the outputs the job actually declares; name the dropped keys and the reason in the file.
3. Add arms for the half the deleted spec never asserted: the stale-head guard and the `run_unit` docs/content classification.
4. Pin the declared output set, so a suite added back reds here first instead of being silently unasserted.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` | #17922 AC-1; sibling precedent `check-chore-sync.spec.mjs` | evaluates the committed `scope` script against mocked Actions globals | none — a classifier gating all of CI without a spec is the defect | spec header | each arm red against a seeded mutation of `test.yml` |
| `jobs.changes` declared outputs | `.github/workflows/test.yml` | exactly `run_unit`, `run_components`, `skip_reason` | n/a | spec header | first arm asserts the key set |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` exists under `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/` and passes against the live `test.yml`.
- [ ] Every arm is shown **red** against a seeded mutation of the workflow it reads — a restored spec that cannot fail is not restored coverage. Mutations must cover, at minimum: fail-closed on an undeterminable diff, fork-blind head resolution, a dropped `learn/` admission, a neutered stale-head guard, and a dropped self-classification.
- [ ] The file names the assertions it dropped and why, so the difference from the deleted original is auditable rather than invisible.
- [ ] The declared-output set is asserted directly, not implied by the other arms.
- [ ] The `unit` project's collected spec-file count rises by exactly 1, measured by count.
- [ ] #17922's body is corrected so its two already-delivered residual rows no longer read as owed.

## Out of Scope

- **The other four residuals** — `check-theme-surfaces`, `RebuildContentIndexesAndSeo`, `PublishReleaseNoteOrphan`, `WorkflowConcurrency`. Each needs its own rewrite-vs-retire judgement; `WorkflowConcurrency` is the natural next one (same harness, same subject file) and is deliberately left unclaimed.
- **Changing what the classifier does.** Restoration is not the moment to fix the subject. If an arm reveals a defect, it gets filed, not patched here.
- **Making `spec-retirement-lint.yml` blocking** — #17171 owns required-context binding for the whole `*-lint.yml` family.

## Avoided Traps

- **Restoring verbatim to get a fast green.** Seven arms would red on outputs that correctly no longer exist, and "fixing" that by deleting assertions without saying so reproduces #17922 in miniature.
- **Restoring to the old `ai/` path.** That prefix is the deletion trigger.
- **Treating a green run as evidence.** The whole finding is that green survived the loss of 804 specs; the honest instruments here are the spec-file count and the mutation ledger.
- **Asserting `run_integration` because the original did.** The original was right when it was written; the topology moved under it.
